cands.name: Jimmy Patronis
cands.bio: Republican, born 1972 in Panama City. Florida House 2006-2014, Public Service Commission 2015-2017, Florida Chief Financial Officer 2017-2025 (appointed by Gov. Rick Scott, then elected twice). Won the April 2025 special election for FL-1 after Matt Gaetz resigned; sworn in April 2, 2025.
cands.local_ties: Panama City native; family has run the Captain Anderson's seafood restaurant there since 1967 (per Wikipedia, 'citation needed'). A January 2025 WKRG report cited by Wikipedia said his wife and children are registered to vote in the neighboring 2nd district (he claims residency in the 1st).

record.text: Committee assignments in Congress: Transportation and Infrastructure; Small Business (official House bio).
Served as Florida CFO June 30, 2017 to March 31, 2025; resigned to run for Congress. Won 2018 (52-48) and 2022 (59.5-40.5) statewide elections.
As a state official he advocated PTSD legislation expanding mental-health benefits for first responders, and worked on a 2019 firefighter cancer-relief bill (his official bio and Wikipedia).

money_notes.text: Crypto-industry super PAC Defend American Jobs spent $345,000 supporting Patronis in the April 2025 special election and more than $200,000 in the special-election primary (Cointelegraph, March 21, 2025). Not a statement about the 2026 general.

In 2017-18 his political committee Treasure Florida accepted contributions from insurance firms Simple Health ($35,000 and $15,000) and Health Benefits One ($10,000) that later faced fraud allegations; his campaign said it did not know and would donate the money to charity (per Wikipedia).

controversies.text: 2017-18: his PAC accepted contributions from two insurers later accused of fraud (Simple Health later faced a $195 million FTC judgment in 2024); the campaign said it was unaware and would give the money to charity.

2019-2020: former financial regulator Ronald Rubin alleged a pay-to-play scheme and asked for a criminal investigation; Florida paid $150,000 in Dec 2019 to settle a harassment complaint. Patronis's office disputes the allegations; the source reports no criminal charges or final ruling.
2023-24: he promoted using up to $5 million in taxpayer funds toward Donald Trump's legal bills; a bill was filed but withdrawn in January 2024 after Gov. DeSantis threatened a veto.
Residency: his wife and children were reported registered in the 2nd district rather than the 1st (WKRG, Jan 2025, cited by Wikipedia). He says he lives in the 1st.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (endorsed him on Nov 25, 2024 for the special election; Florida Politics reported a renewed Trump endorsement Oct 25, 2025 - that page is paywalled and was not opened).
AIPAC and the NRA Political Victory Fund are listed as endorsers on the Wikipedia 2026 district page (citing aipacpac.org and nrapvf.org; those pages were not opened).

cands.gaps: Photo skipped per brief. No state roll-call votes (FL House 2006-2014) gathered. No 2026 general-election outside-spending totals found. Wikipedia text for his House tenure was thin; sponsored bills not verified. District 1 is unchanged by the 2026 map (WUSF); official bio lists Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa and Walton counties.

votes.what: Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.
Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

cands.name: Gay Valimont
cands.bio: Democrat, Pensacola. Former athletic trainer (sports medicine in Atlanta), then gun-violence-prevention volunteer and organizer; rose to Moms Demand Action Florida chapter lead. Third run for this seat: lost to Matt Gaetz in 2024 and to Jimmy Patronis in the April 2025 special election. Has not held public office.
cands.local_ties: Lives in Pensacola; returned to the area after 2020. Degrees from Georgia Southern University and Troy State University (campaign bio).

record.text: Nominee in the April 2025 special election; lost to Patronis 97,370 to 72,375 votes.

Campaign priorities: public safety and gun-violence prevention, affordable health care, public schools, rising food/housing/insurance costs; has said she wants a full-service VA hospital for the region.

endorsements.text: Democratic Progressive Caucus of Florida; National Women's Political Caucus; Progressive Democrats of America (per Wikipedia 2026 district page citing Florida Phoenix, nwpc.org, pdamerica.org).

cands.gaps: No fundraising/outside-money details verified. Florida Phoenix page for the progressive-caucus endorsement was cited by Wikipedia but returned 403 so it was not opened.
